meta.title: Ignacio Garbayo — CV
meta.description: Software Engineer with a dual foundation in Computer Engineering and Mathematics.

summary.title: Summary
summary.content: Software Engineer with a dual foundation in Computer Engineering and Mathematics. Proven experience building predictive classification models for medical research and integrating real-time data flows to optimize decision-making. Engineered complex optimization solutions, including a scheduling engine and an AI/IoT water management system. Led the development of a Business Intelligence algorithm awarded 1st prize nationwide by Bankinter.

bullets: Relevant Courses: Algorithms and Data Structures (C), Computer Architecture, Object Oriented Programming (Java), Formal Languages and Automata Theory, Intelligent Systems and Artificial Intelligence (Python), Cybersecurity
Final thesis: Computer Vision & Artificial Intelligence
Grade: 8.1/10
Relevant Courses: Linear and Multilinear Algebra, Numerical Methods in Optimization and Differential Equations, General Topology, Probability and Statistics, Inference and Multivariate Analysis (R)
Final thesis: Advanced classification models for epidemiological research
Grade: 7.7/10
Courses finished with honours: Statistical Inference

entries.title: Research Intern
bullets: Summer Research Fellow, focused on Computer Vision. Architected multimodal semantic grounding pipelines and leveraged foundation models to advance open-world object discovery.

entries.title: Intern, Full Stack Development
bullets: Focused on high availability of applications, I manage the full lifecycle of projects, from requirements definition to CI/CD automation (Docker, Kubernetes, Jenkins). Currently architecting a Change Data Capture pipeline with Apache Flink and Redis, designed to stream thousands of product updates to OTAs per minute.

Secured OTA data consistency and reduced debugging hours by developing a NestJS, Angular, and MongoDB web app to visualize RabbitMQ/Kafka data flows, later bringing a Redpanda-powered monitor to expose performance metrics and anomalies.
Minimized initial Kafka service's queue lag by creating a horizontal autoscaling microservice using Docker to dynamically provision specialized consumers on demand, separating by topics.

entries.title: Intern, Machine Learning
bullets: Optimized supervised classification models in R (caret, caretEnsemble) and Python, mitigating overfitting to achieve a robust accuracy of 88%.
Developed static and dynamic classifier ensembles for breast cancer prediction, encompassing data preparation, feature selection, threshold tuning, model training, and metric analysis.
Leveraged caretStack, DESLib, and KNORA to evaluate the accuracy of various base and mixed models.

entries.title: Basketball Referee & Tutor
bullets: Demonstrated decision-making under pressure, effective communication, teamwork, and attention to detail by refereeing in the 1st regional division and four Spanish Championships (U12/U14 Regional Teams, U14/U16 Clubs).

Training new officials as a referee tutor by conducting performance reviews and teaching rules, mechanics, and conflict resolution on the court, preparing them for weekly assignments and high-stress situations.

entries.title: [Akademia](https://www.fundacionbankinter.org/nuestras-iniciativas/akademia-future-builders/) winner and mentor
bullets: Selected as one of 80 participants nationwide for a 4-month tech innovation program featuring expert debates. Led the ML development of an impactful Business Intelligence algorithm for a real-world business case, winning first prize. Later selected as a mentor, guiding another team to win the subsequent edition.

entries.title: 3rd Prize, Best Essay on AI Applications
Honors Distinction, High & Secondary School
bullets: Highest university entrance exam score in the Province of Ourense (13.92/14).

entries.title: Hackathons
bullets: Won the Alén Space Challenge and 2nd Best Open Source Project at HackUDC 2026 (400+ participants) with BFG-I. Selected from 1,700+ applicants to participate in HackUPC 2026 with XEITECH. Both projects were developed under 36-hour constraints.

**HackUDC** ([BFG-I](https://github.com/YagoFalgueras/HackUDC-2026)): Built a satellite-to-ground DOOM streaming system over simulated LEO links in C, using H.264 video compression, RTP/UDP packetization, and a lock-free ring buffer.

**HackUPC** ([XEITECH](https://github.com/igarbayo/HackUPC-2026)): Developed an automated warehouse simulator with a heuristics-driven I/O algorithm, SSTF instruction reordering, and a 3D digital twin using C++, Python, and React.

entries.title: Open Source Governance Skill
bullets: A skill in the Agent Skills format for Claude Code and OpenCode that sets up the complete open source governance of a project, generating the license, the REUSE metadata and the contributing, security and CI artifacts that follow FSF and OSI best practices.
It was born as a utility to release a hackathon project, but it works for any kind of project.

entries.title: Automated Referee Assignments
bullets: Engineered an optimization engine in Python to efficiently schedule up to 800 weekly matches, combining personnel scheduling and vehicle routing problems.
Resolved complex constraints including schedule overlaps, conflict vetoes, and skill-level matching through weighted greedy selection, complemented by local search and geometric approximations.

entries.title: Smart Water Management
bullets: Developing an AI/IoT platform (NestJS, R, React) with two Bankinter Akademia colleagues for small Galician municipalities, aiming to optimize natural resources and reduce Non-Revenue Water leaks.
The solution, an anomaly detection algorithm based on an unsupervised ensemble, is currently being prototyped ahead of planned municipal pilot tests.

entries.title: Student Magazine
bullets: Editor and contributor for a monthly Math Faculty magazine at the University of Santiago de Compostela.
Collaborated closely to publish high-quality technical and outreach content, expanding my skillset by exploring topics beyond the standard curriculum.
Published in [Minerva](https://minerva.usc.gal/collections/a66d5c8e-d4d0-49f5-95fc-a41bd831140d).

entries.title: Refugees volunteering
entries.description: Taught refugees basketball rules and refereeing values as a representative of the Galician Basketball Federation in the Basket Bridges program, in collaboration with NGO Rescate & ADB Fontiñas.

entries.title: Social volunteering
entries.description: Organized and distributed food, assisted in community dining programs, and provided presents and clothing to children in need as part of the school-based NGO "10%" of Maristas Ourense.

entries.title: Introduction to Open Source License Compliance Management (LFC193)
AWS Cloud Practitioner Training Badge
bullets: Worked in several cases with foundational cloud computing tools in AWS Cloud.
Developed practical expertise by learning core concepts in computing, networking, security, and storage.

entries.title: AWS Generative AI Practitioner Training Badge
bullets: Applied hands-on skills in prompt engineering, code generation, chatbot development, content moderation systems and fine-tuning models to optimize performance using AWS AI services.

entries.title: AI Agents Fundamentals
bullets: Demonstrated practical knowledge of AI agents, including tools, actions, observations, and data formats.
Worked with large language models (LLMs), messages, special tokens and chat templates.
